source: He had a 2 cm laceration above the left eyebrow, bruising of the left eye, abrasion of the right hand, dislocation of the left elbow, and a Colles fracture of the left radius.
The broken arm was in a plaster cast for six weeks The Plaintiff was discharged after two weeks and attended regularly at the Sai Ying Pun Clinic until late October, 1981.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture at other specified part of wrist or hand level

source: He was transferred to the university Orthopaedic Unit at Queen Mary Hospital where the dislocation was reduced and he was found to have mild left medial nerve palsy.
The median nerve traverses the front of the elbow and was crushed in the dislocation, resulting in median nerve palsy.
There was a permanent loss of median nerve function.
Wrist movement is now normal but median nerve supply to the forearm muscles has not improved at all. Further recovery of muscle power cannot take place.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of median nerve at forearm level

injuries.description: The Plaintiff had cerebral oedema which was treated with steroids.
source: The Plaintiff had cerebral oedema which was treated with steroids.
The first report showed that the Plaintiff suffered concussion and also post traumatic amnesia lasting four days.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with incomplete loss of consciousness with amnesia

manifestations.description: The Plaintiff was rendered unconscious by the accident
post traumatic amnesia lasting four days
Post concussional symptoms consisted of dizziness
severe headaches (post-concussional); by September 1981 one mild headache of about four minutes duration once a week
There had been some bleeding into the left eye but it had cleared up, leaving the vision unaffected.
loss of sensation in the thumb and these fingers
wasting of the Thenar Eminence (the muscular swelling in the palm on the thumb side)
lost the final 5o of straightening the arm at the elbow though flexion was normal
Wrist movement was normal save that forward flexion was reduced from 80o to 60o
could not perform fine movements of finger and thumb as well as he could on the right hand
The Plaintiff was found to have an 80 lb grip with his right hand but only a 10 lb grip with his left
There was considerable wasting of the forearm muscles. The measurement round the right forearm was 10" and, round the left, 9".

2% impairment of the arm from the left wrist, a 2% impairment from loss of elbow joint movement and a 10% impairment of the arm from the median nerve loss. A 14% impairment of the arm was said by Dr. Wedderburn to be a 6% impairment of the whole man.
There was a permanent loss of median nerve function.
The loss of movement of extending the arm at the elbow had increased from 5o to 8o, the impairment having increased to 3%.
Wrist movement is now normal but median nerve supply to the forearm muscles has not improved at all. Further recovery of muscle power cannot take place.
The Plaintiff has pain in his arm and occasionally has to take a day or two off work.
There is mild osteo-arthritis of the elbow

treatments_received: physiotherapy three times a week for two and a half months
treatment with steroids for cerebral oedema
outpatient attendance at Sai Ying Pun Clinic

losses.description: Recurrent pain in his arm as well as loss of function in his elbow and grip in his hand.

His market value as a decorating worker is affected; he cannot do outside work (e.g. painting the outside of buildings) because of poor grip in the left hand; inability to work a full month because of recurrent pain means he must rely on casual work and loses five days a month on average.

comparable_cases.injury_description: Fracture of left radius and dislocation of left ulna. Loss of 10 lb grip in the left (unpreferred) hand. 8% impairment of the left arm and 5% impairment of the whole man.

Lacerations to the right hand, fracture of 2nd and 5th metacarpal bones, and rupture of the extensor tendon to index and middle fingers. Two operations were carried out. Stiffness to the fingers of the dominant hand, loss of grip and pinching function and loss of dexterity.

Amputation at the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right index finger as a result of a crushing injury. Loss of use of the index finger and loss of grip in the right hand, giving a permanent disability of 10%.
